headline: Mortgage-sale charge drives a loss; adjusted profit steady
summary_short: First Horizon's Q3 2026 net loss to common was $94M (-$0.20/share) after a $347M after-tax hit from a pending mortgage sale; adjusted EPS was $0.53.
summary_long: Reported results include notable items of $0.73 per share, mainly from reclassifying about $4.5B of lower-yielding consumer mortgages to held for sale; the company agreed in early October to sell them. Adjusted EPS of $0.53 was down $0.01 q/q and up $0.02 y/y. Net interest income rose $7M to $686M with NIM at 3.48%. Net charge-offs were 22 bps. CET1 fell to 10.3% on the reclassification. The sale is expected to settle early in Q4 and be accretive going forward.
confidence_notes: The 8-K cover has no EX-99 exhibit in its folder index; the earnings release document in the same filing was used. Reported figures are GAAP; adjusted EPS excludes notable items. Revenue is shown on a fully taxable-equivalent basis as the release headlines it.

drivers.explanation: A loss tied to reclassifying select mortgage loans to held for sale ahead of the pending portfolio sale drove the reported loss.
Higher average loan yield of 5.73% lifted NII; margin slipped on higher interest-bearing deposit costs.
The decline was driven by notable items, mainly the mortgage held-for-sale reclassification.
CEO pointed to a $1.3B rise in average client deposits and a focus on deploying capital for long-term value.
